title: Budget gating + probabilistic-eviction-aware routing for GPU & spot/on-demand selection
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: We need a routing layer that simultaneously enforces per-customer budget caps, chooses between spot and on-demand instances, and selects GPU classes by optimizing for cost-per-token while respecting latency SLOs and eviction risk. Current router reacts too late to spot evictions and has coarse spend guards that lead to sudden rate limiting when budgets are hit.

Goal: Implement a policy scorer and gating layer that: 1) computes a real-time cost-reliability score per candidate (region, instance SKU, model variant), 2) enforces sliding-window budget caps at request-routing time instead of post-hoc throttles, and 3) uses probabilistic spot-eviction forecasts to prefer on-demand or lower-risk SKUs before degradation occurs. The layer must support model-variant fallbacks (quantized / smaller models) based on customer tier and quality budgets.

Design summary:
- Policy Scorer: score = w_cost * normalized_cost_per_token + w_latency * estimated_tail_ms + w_eviction * eviction_risk - w_quality * model_quality_delta. We will compute normalized values from telemetry histograms and up-to-date price catalog. Weights are per-customer and tied to plan (free/dev/standard/enterprise).
- Eviction risk model: lightweight time-series that combines historical eviction rate per SKU-region, current spot pool headroom metric, and short-term cloud signal (e.g., preemption metric). Output is a probability in [0,1].
- Budget gating: sliding-window charge aggregation (default 1h/24h windows) stored in fast cache (redis with TTL + consistent hashing). At routing time, the scorer will compute projected spend for request and reject or downgrade if projected window spend would exceed cap. Downgrades include routing to quantized model, switching to on-demand, or returning a quota-exceeded error depending on customer config.
- Fallback policy: prioritized list per request: same-variant cheaper instance -> quantized variant in same region -> same-variant on on-demand -> smaller-latency-preserving model variant -> error. Fallback decisions are recorded as structured events for Quality monitoring.
- Compatibility: policy is opt-in per-customer; default weights for existing customers preserve current routing behavior. Admin console exposes per-customer weight overrides and budget cap settings.

Acceptance criteria:
- Benchmarks show median router decision latency < 15ms added overhead.
- In simulation (traffic replay for 7 days), system maintains customer hourly spend <= cap for 99.9% of windows without returning >1% unexpected 429s for pay-tier customers.
- Spot-eviction preemption rate for routed requests reduces by >= 60% compared to baseline (measured as fraction of requests that experienced eviction-caused fallback).
- End-to-end Canary: deploy to 5% of traffic and observe no regression in 99th percentile latency beyond configured SLOs.

Operational concerns:
- Telemetry: need new metrics: policy_score_histogram, eviction_risk_estimate, budget_projection_decisions, fallback_reason. These must be instrumented with dimensions: customer_id, region, sku, model_variant.
- State store: budget windows must be resilient to race conditions; use optimistic increment with Lua script in Redis or small consistent microservice to manage windows.
- Simulation: create traffic replay harness with sampled historical requests and cloud spot eviction traces to evaluate policy behavior.

Open design trade-offs:
- Where to compute score: inside router process (low latency) vs external policy service (easier to change). We will implement a thin local scorer with periodically refreshed model parameters to avoid RPC overhead.
- Eviction forecasting accuracy vs complexity: start with simple heuristic + exponential smoothing; iterate to ML model if needed.

Rollout plan:
1) Unit tests + off-line simulator (2 weeks)
2) Local router + feature flag (opt-in) in staging with synthetic high-eviction scenarios (1 week)
3) Canary to 5% of small customers (2 weeks)
4) Expand to all non-enterprise customers while observing metrics (2 weeks)
5) Enterprise opt-in and admin console controls (concurrent)

Security & compliance: budget window keys will be keyed by customer-id masked; no sensitive PII stored. Ensure KMS-protected credentials for price catalog fetches.

Backward compatibility: default weights make behavior unchanged for customers who don't opt-in. API surfaces unchanged; console exposes additional toggles.

Deliverables:
- router/scorer implementation (go)
- eviction risk library (go)
- redis windowing helper + Lua scripts
- simulator & harness + dashboards
- console controls and README

2026-03-10 - Design review with Product and Console: added per-customer weight overrides and admin visibility. PM Rafael requested a safe default that never returns 4xx/spend errors for enterprise customers - we will honor that via 'enterprise_grace' flag.

2026-03-11 - Simulation day 1: replayed 72h of traffic with synthetic spot-loss spikes. Preliminary result: projected spend gating prevented 95% of spent overshoot events; eviction reduction ~50%. Need to tune weights and window size.
2026-03-12 - PR opened for local scorer core: github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/412 (prototype). Requesting review from @sre-team and @runtime-team.
